captions.instagram:
The Gloria Tornado.

I'm six, sitting on a tiny raised seat in the middle of the back row, right next to my little brother's car seat. The road ahead is miles of winding dirt. We're late, of course.

Swipe through.

From Not Plain. Read it at the link in bio.

pinterest.description: A six-year-old's memory from the back seat of a forest green Pontiac on a winding Texas dirt road, told as memoir. Narrative nonfiction about family and memory from Not Plain, a memoir newsletter by Sarah.

slides.text: It’s a hot summer day. My family is living in a small Texas town, and I’m 6 years old.

slides.label: the road
slides.text: The road is lined with blackberry bushes and overgrown trees

slides.label: the car
slides.text: Finally, she loads us into the forest green Pontiac.

slides.label: the backseat
slides.text: …a tiny raised middle seat between us.

slides.label: winding dirt road
slides.text: We start the drive from our house down the miles-long winding dirt road
We haven’t gone far when the car screeches to a halt.
